name: Turkmen
notes: Turkmen in the Latin alphabet official since 1993. The letter values follow Gray's orthography-to-IPA table (§2.2): ⟨s⟩ and ⟨z⟩ are the interdental fricatives /θ ð/, the feature that separates Turkmen from every other Turkic standard (the alveolar [s z] readings are the Charjew dialect and are kept as allophones); ⟨y⟩ is the close back unrounded vowel /ɯ/ and ⟨ý⟩ is /j/, not the Turkish assignment of ⟨y⟩ to /j/; ⟨r⟩ is a flap /ɾ/ that becomes a trill when written double (garry); ⟨g⟩ is a stop word-initially and a fricative /ɣ/ elsewhere. ⟨ä⟩ is always long (§2.3), the one length contrast the orthography does encode: length is otherwise phonemic but unwritten, so this spec cannot and does not predict it. Ä = /æː/, Ň = /ŋ/, W is a labial-velar approximant, Ž = /ʒ/ in Russian loanwords. ⟨a⟩ is left as /a/: Gray's harmony chart classes it back while his pronunciation gloss describes a front vowel, and the two shipped golds disagree on the symbol, so the choice is not decidable from the source.

stress.notes: Turkmen default stress is word-final (-1). Some grammatical suffixes (negation, question) attract stress to their own syllable; not modeled here. Source: Comrie (1997) in Johanson & Csató.
